full_judgment: 6. SM Shahjahan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that there is no motive in the present case for the purpose of committing murder of the victim and that the petitioner had no earthly reason to kill him and that the witnesses were not also sure about the appearance of the petitioner, such confusing statement cannot be considered as positive evidence and it is not possible on the part of the persons who saw the occurrence to identify the accused-petitioner in a positive manner; that the motive alleged for the murder by the convict-petitioner does not inspire confidence in view of the fact that in the absence of any motive the killing of the victim by the petitioner does not support the prosecution case save and except a doubt created in the mind of the relations of the victim which the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to consider in convicting the petitioner; that investigating officer of the case seized knife, blood stained clothes and pitch during the investigation and accordingly prepared the seizure list of those materials but the prosecution did not produce those seized materials before the pitch and such non-production of these alamats call in question the veracity of the prosecution and such with-holding of those materials to be produced by the prosecution gave rise to an adverse presumption against the findings of conviction of the leave petitioner. The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that there are inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of PW's 2, 3 and 4 as to the manner of stabbing the victim inasmuch as their evidence is not consistent with the medical report, thus there is serious doubt as to their witnessing the occurrence and that Hiran, in front of whose shop the occurrence took place, was material witness while the prosecution without any explanation withheld him and for this non-examination, presumption would be that had he been examined he would not support the prosecution case; that the High Court Division did not consider that witnessing the occurrence by PW 4 who was inside his shop at the relevant time, is utmost doubtful as staying inside the shop it was impracticable for him to witness the occurrence took place in front of the shop of Hiran, the place of occurrence was shifted by PW 2 who said that the occurrence took place in front of his shop although the place of occurrence shown in the sketch map by the letter 'Kha' is in front of the shop of Hiran, not in front of his shop shown by the letter 'Gha' and that the shop of Sentu shown by letter 'Gha" in the sketch map is situated to the opposite of the shop of Hiran to the other side of the road and that the shop of PW 2 is not the opposite of the shop of Hiran. Thus the evidence of PW 2 that the occurrence took place in front of his shop makes his evidence as an incredible eye-witness, therefore, the prosecution could not prove the charge beyond all reasonable doubt against the petitioner and, as such, the petitioner is entitled to benefit of doubt and ought to have been acquitted of the charge.
